Abstract:

This thesis focuses on the design of plant-derived antibacterial hydrogel platforms for infected wound management. Different crosslinking strategies have been employed to fabricate hydrogel networks to achieve enhanced mechanical stability and self-healing ability, thereby reinforcing structural integrity. Plant extracts were employed as sustainable capping and stabilizing agents for the green synthesis of nanoparticles. Incorporation of these plant-derived components endowed the hydrogel systems with antioxidant activity and potent antibacterial efficacy while maintaining excellent cytocompatibility toward normal cell lines. Furthermore, additional treatment modalities, including photothermal therapy and nitric oxide (NO) gas therapy, were integrated to enhance the overall efficacy of the hydrogel system. Finally, the therapeutic potential of the developed antibacterial hydrogels was evaluated using both in vitro and in vivo wound-healing models, demonstrating their promising potential for infected wound management.
